title: Quantum Reinforcement Learning for Cost and Delay Tradeoffs in Quantum Cloud Orchestration
authors: An N. H. Phan, Dang Van Huynh, Muhammad Usman, Hoa T. Nguyen
abstract: Quantum cloud computing, delivered through the quantum-as-a-service (QaaS) model, provides access to quantum computing resources. However, applying uniform time-based pricing across fundamentally heterogeneous quantum resources significantly complicates task orchestration, particularly when addressing the tradeoff between execution costs and system performance. While heuristic methods rely on predefined scheduling rules, classical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models may require more trainable parameters in this setting. Motivated by the potential of parameterised quantum circuits (PQCs) as compact function approximators, we propose QRLQ, a cost-delay-aware quantum cloud scheduling framework integrating PQCs with a dueling double deep Q-network (D3QN) to dynamically account for both cost and delay. Our simulation results show that QRLQ achieves lower mean cost and delay than the heuristic baselines, achieving a 5-11% lower mean cost relative to availability-based and rotation-based heuristics and reducing mean delay by 17% and 82% relative to the strongest and weakest heuristic baselines, respectively, while retaining execution fidelity within 2% of a fidelity-greedy policy. Compared with the classical DRL baseline, QRLQ achieves comparable scheduling performance while using 72% fewer trainable parameters. This work explores the feasibility of using QRL for task orchestration in quantum cloud environments and demonstrates its potential for cost-delay-aware quantum resource management.
summary: This paper introduces QRLQ, a quantum reinforcement learning framework designed to optimally schedule quantum tasks across heterogeneous quantum cloud resources. By integrating Parameterized Quantum Circuits with a D3QN, QRLQ effectively manages the critical trade-off between minimizing execution cost and reducing overall system delay. The results demonstrate that QRLQ offers superior performance compared to existing heuristics while being significantly more parameter-efficient than classical deep RL methods.
main_problem: The paper addresses the complex task of orchestrating quantum cloud computing resources (QaaS) by jointly minimizing execution costs and system delays.
main_result: The proposed QRLQ framework significantly outperforms heuristic baselines by achieving lower mean cost and substantial reductions in mean delay while maintaining high execution fidelity.
method: It proposes QRLQ, a novel framework that integrates Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQCs) with a Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN) for decision-making.
model_or_system: The system models a heterogeneous quantum cloud environment composed of multiple Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) accessed via a QaaS model. The problem is formulated as an online sequential decision process (MDP).
key_observables: Mean Cost, Mean Delay, Execution Fidelity, Execution Time, and Waiting Time.
important_parameters: Qubit count, quantum volume, gate error rates, and the weighting factors ($\eta$) used in the scheduling score calculation.
main_assumptions: The work assumes a uniform time-based pricing model and is motivated by the constraints of the NISQ era, though it aims for future fault-tolerant environments.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the system workflow (Fig. 2) and compare average execution time and waiting time across various scheduling policies (Fig. 6a-d).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem setup, details the QRLQ methodology integrating PQCs into D3QN, presents the cost/delay objective function, and validates the approach through extensive simulations comparing QRLQ against multiple heuristic and classical DRL baselines.
why_interesting: While focused on cloud orchestration, the use of PQCs as compact function approximators for complex resource management decisions is a key topic at the intersection of quantum machine learning and quantum networking.

Fig. 2. System-level workflow of the proposed QRLQ framework for cost-delay-aware resource orchestration.

Fig. 2 illustrates the system-level workflow of the proposed QRLQ framework within a heterogeneous QaaS environment. The architecture consists of a centralised broker managed by the QRLQ orchestrator and a set of heterogeneous quantum nodes (QNodes) to process user-submitted quantum tasks (QTasks). Each QTask includes an abstract circuit with specific technical characteristics. Initially, a feature extractor processes this circuit to extract key task features. By evaluating these task features alongside the dynamic QNode states, the QRLQ core allocates each QTask to the QNode with the highest estimated action value. Fig. 3. Example of quantum circuit transpilation and its DAG representation for execution time and execution fidelity estimation.

Figure 3 illustrates the processing of a QTask by quantum computing resources and the associated circuit compilation process. The abstract circuit, shown in the left panel, must be compiled and mapped to the physical qubit topology of the target quantum hardware, such as the ibm_sydney system depicted in the centre panel. This procedure produces a transpiled circuit, represented as a DAG in the right panel. Notably, the DAG of the transpiled circuit enables execution time estimation via the critical path using operation times Tj, and supports fidelity evaluation through error probabilities Ej.
